summary: fca-raihan routes Facebook credentials and 2FA secrets to third-party endpoint minhdong.site
details: The package advertises itself as a Facebook chat client but its email/password login path POSTs the caller's Facebook email, password, and 2FA Base32 secret to a hardcoded author-controlled endpoint at https://minhdong.site/api/v1/facebook/login_ios (module/config.js sets `apiServer: "https://minhdong.site"` as the default `baseUrl`). The endpoint returns Facebook session cookies and access tokens to the client, meaning the author-operated server observes every user's Facebook credentials and resulting session material and can retain them. Callers of `login({ email, password, twoFactor })` do not opt into a third-party proxy — the destination is baked in and is not Facebook's own auth infrastructure, so the credential crosses the issuer trust boundary to a host under the maintainer's control. Additionally, `package.json` declares a self-referential dependency `"fca-raihan": "github:raihan9099/fca-raihan"` with no commit SHA or tag pin, so `npm install` clones the default branch of that GitHub repo at install time; whoever controls that repo can ship arbitrary code to installers independently of npm registry versioning.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
